title: Solo Egypt Itinerary: 7 Days With Shared Day Tours

The quick answer

A good 7-day solo Egypt itinerary runs Cairo, Luxor, Aswan in that order: three nights in Cairo for Giza and the old capital's pyramids, two in Luxor for its temples and tombs, and one in Aswan before an early start for Abu Simbel and an evening flight out. Buy the sightseeing as shared day tours (five tours from €241 per person in total, as listed in November 2026) and keep arrival and flight days free. Solo travellers pay the same per-person price as everyone else on the departure.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

Travelling alone in Egypt raises two questions at once: what do I see in one week, and who do I see it with? Private guides answer the second by pricing for a pair or a vehicle; big bus tours answer it by herding dozens of people past the Sphinx. This itinerary takes a third road: two independent days and five sightseeing days bought as shared day tours. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace, pools travellers onto those dates, and our team has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Solo Egypt itinerary, 7 days: the route at a glance

Seven days give you Egypt's three essential stops, Cairo, Luxor and Aswan, in one southbound line with no backtracking. Two days are arrival and travel days; five are sightseeing days, each bought as a shared day tour with a licensed guide. You fly from Cairo to Luxor, ride the temple road down to Aswan, and fly out of Aswan on the last evening.

Why this order works

Cairo first puts the pyramids next to your international airport. The short hop south to Luxor (about an hour in the air) lands you in temple country, and the road day to Aswan turns a transfer into sightseeing at Edfu and Kom Ombo. Finishing in Aswan lines up the trip's grand finale, Abu Simbel, and repeats no leg of the journey. It also puts the hardest early start, the very early Abu Simbel pickup, on your last morning.

Day by day: Cairo, Luxor and Aswan in one week

Every sightseeing day below is a Sawa tour as described on its listing. Reserve a seat on each tour free of charge; nothing is charged until the date confirms. The two travel days are left deliberately empty.

Prices are per person, as listed in November 2026, and fixed per traveller however the group fills. Check pickup details for your own date on its departure page. For Day 2, our guide to the pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day shows how to fit the museum in.

Swap-ins if you have more or fewer days

With an eighth day or a late flight, two additions slot in cleanly. The Aswan Highlights morning (Unfinished Obelisk, High Dam and Philae Temple by motorboat, with lunch, about 5 hours, from €36) fits on an extra Aswan day, which is also the way to turn Day 7 into a relaxed one: stay a second night in Aswan and fly out on Day 8. The Secrets of the Grand Egyptian Museum tour (about 3 hours, from €48) fills Day 2's afternoon. With only six days, cut the Memphis, Saqqara and Dahshur day and fly south a morning earlier; Giza alone carries Cairo's pyramid quota.

Is Egypt safe for a solo traveller?

Nowhere is risk-free, and the official advice says so. As of 8 November 2026 the UK Foreign Office, the US State Department (Level 2, "Exercise Increased Caution") and the Government of Canada all advise caution in Egypt because of terrorism. All three name areas to avoid, including North Sinai, the Libyan border region and parts of the Western Desert; the UK's exceptions to its Western Desert warning include Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel and the Valley of the Kings, which this route uses. The UK describes the crime rate as generally low and asks visitors to take sensible precautions. Read your own government's page in the week you book, because the advice changes and your insurance may depend on it.

This itinerary keeps you in company where a solo traveller wants it:

  • The group is part of the structure. A shared departure puts you with up to seven fellow travellers, a guide who knows the terrain and a fixed itinerary on the sightseeing days. That reduces lone decisions at remote sites; it does not remove risk.
  • Early starts are the honest trade. Abu Simbel leaves very early because the temples sit roughly 280 km from Aswan on a desert road with routine checkpoints (carry your passport); Luxor's full day starts early to beat the heat.
  • Keep the ordinary habits. Agree taxi prices first, keep valuables discreet, dress modestly at village stops, and skip empty streets late at night. Solo women should also read the UK and Canadian guidance on harassment and travelling alone at night.

Each tour is run by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due, and every guided tour has a licensed guide.

At EGP 60 to the euro (8 November 2026), those entrance fees are small beside the tours, but they are what catch budgets out. Grand Egyptian Museum tickets are sold online only, at tickets.gem.eg, so buy yours in advance.

Why mix independent days with shared day tours?

Because five guided days in a row exhaust anyone, and Egypt rewards slow hours as much as monuments. The two independent days cost nothing, let you set your own pace, and make the guided days feel like events rather than a conveyor belt. They are also your buffer: if a flight slips or a site closes, an empty day absorbs it.

  • Day 1 in Cairo. Walk Khan el-Khalili's lanes, drink mint tea under the arches, and keep the evening early; the Giza tour starts next morning.
  • Day 4 in Luxor. Luxor Temple sits in the middle of town and stays open into the evening, so a late-afternoon visit works after a morning flight. Check the hours on the day.
  • Day 6 in Aswan. The temple road takes about 6.5 hours, so you reach Aswan with time to spare: hire a felucca (a traditional wooden sailboat) for the golden hour, or simply watch the boats from the Corniche. Go to bed early; Abu Simbel leaves very early.

Sawa Tours is a shared-departure marketplace, not a tour operator. Sawa runs a fixed catalogue with its own calendar and prices; agencies sell the seats; and each departure is run by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Among them is a founding operating partner, Capital Travel Service (licence 2179).

Pick a forming date or start your own, which we review first; reserving a seat costs nothing and needs no card. When a date reaches four travellers it gets the GoAhead and a 10% deposit is due by payment link. The balance is due two days (48 hours) before departure. A forming date has until seven days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and we suggest another date. Groups never exceed eight. A traveller who cancels more than 48 hours before departure gets a full refund; within 48 hours the 10% deposit is retained; a force majeure event such as riots or a revolution brings a full refund. Payment is by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros.

Because these are five separate departures, book your flights only after each date confirms. Browse forming and confirmed departures to see which dates are already close to their GoAhead, or read how the GoAhead works. The verdict: seven days, one route, no solo supplement

One week is enough for Egypt's essential triangle (Cairo's pyramids, Luxor's tombs, Aswan's temples and Abu Simbel) if the sightseeing is organised and the travel days stay empty. This route buys five shared day tours for €241, confirms each date at four travellers, and never charges a solo traveller extra. faq.q: What is a good 7-day Egypt itinerary for a solo traveller?
faq.a: Cairo first (Days 1 to 3): the Giza pyramids, then Memphis, Saqqara and Dahshur. Luxor next (Days 4 and 5): one flight day, then a full East and West Bank day. Aswan last (Days 6 and 7): travel down the temple road via Edfu and Kom Ombo, then Abu Simbel on the final morning. Five shared day tours carry the sightseeing, and arrival and flight days stay free: €241 per person in tours, as listed in November 2026.

faq.q: Is Egypt safe to travel alone as a woman?
faq.a: Many solo women travel this route, and its structure helps: guided days with small groups of up to eight. No destination is risk-free, though. As of 8 November 2026 the UK, US and Canadian governments all advise caution in Egypt and name areas to avoid, and the UK and Canadian advice warns about harassment, with the UK advising women to take caution when travelling alone, particularly at night and in taxis. Keep the usual habits: agree taxi prices first, dress modestly at village stops and skip empty streets late at night. Check your government's current advice before booking.

faq.q: Do solo travellers pay more for shared day tours in Egypt?
faq.a: No. On Sawa's day tours the price is fixed per traveller and identical for everyone on the departure; there is no solo surcharge whether you join as one or as part of a group. Reserving a seat is free, and nothing is charged until the date reaches four travellers and confirms (the GoAhead).

faq.q: What happens if my tour date doesn't reach four travellers?
faq.a: A date has until seven days before the tour to reach four. If it does not, it is cancelled and nothing is charged; we suggest another date, or you can start your own date on the tour page. Once a date confirms, it is not cancelled for low numbers.

faq.q: Can I do this route without domestic flights?
faq.a: Partly. The Luxor to Aswan leg is by road anyway, since the Edfu and Kom Ombo day tour covers the journey south. Between Cairo and Luxor you can fly (about an hour in the air) or take the overnight sleeper train, which takes roughly 9 to 10 hours and saves a hotel night; sleeper fares are reported at about US$80 to 100 per person in a shared cabin, more for a single. Most one-week travellers fly at least the Cairo to Luxor leg to protect Day 4's afternoon.

faq.q: How far ahead should I plan a one-week solo trip to Egypt?
faq.a: Reserve tour seats (free) on the dates you want first, because nothing is charged before the GoAhead, then book flights and hotels only after each date confirms. For travel in the cooler months, roughly October to April, start earlier than you think you need to.
